platform.rationale: Platform-first in CSS, HTTP and URL handling, and native form controls. The one duplication of API knowledge is the hand-built sprite URL, a documented-but-fragile shortcut; a fetch timeout/AbortController would also be welcome.

evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts:13 — fetchApi(): Promise<any>; all PokeAPI payloads and return shapes (loadHomeData, loadPokemonPageData, …) are untyped
app/src/lib/queries.ts:4-38 — queries are untyped passthroughs, so the any-ness crosses the server boundary into the client
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].tsx:34,142 — components typed props: { data: any } / props: { table: any }; same in moves/types/abilities routes
app/package.json:5-14 — no devDependencies at all (no typescript, lint, typecheck script) despite tsconfig.json:14 having strict: true, so the TS is never actually checked
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].tsx:15 — double Show (fallback wrapping Show when={data() === null}) conflates loading and not-found; copy-pasted in four routes
app/src/app.css:311 — padding-right with !important to beat the app's own .stats-table td selector
app/src/lib/api.ts:11 — single in-memory promise cache keyed by path; data access is centralized in lib/api.ts + lib/queries.ts (good)
churn_resistance.rationale: Data access is properly centralized behind lib/api.ts and config lives in one file, so a framework upgrade would touch little. But there are effectively no types at the API boundary and no tooling to check the ones written, which is the main source of future churn.

findings.issue: The entire data layer is untyped: fetchApi returns Promise<any>, every loader returns untyped objects, and components re-type them as any (routes/pokemon/[name].tsx:34, routes/types/[name].tsx:24). Payload changes surface as runtime breakage, not type errors.
findings.suggestion: Define interfaces for the PokeAPI payloads and the page-view models in one module and have the loaders and component props use them.

findings.issue: No devDependencies and no typecheck/lint script: tsconfig.json sets strict: true but nothing runs tsc, so the TypeScript is decorative and can silently drift.
findings.suggestion: Add typescript as a devDependency and a `typecheck` script (and ideally a lint/format step) so the strict config is actually enforced in CI.

findings.issue: The 404 page never sets the HTTP status; the framework's HttpStatusCode component is current, the spec says 404 is encouraged, and entry-server.tsx:22 already uses mode "async" which is exactly what makes it work on Node presets.
findings.suggestion: Add `<HttpStatusCode code={404} />` to NotFound (and to the `data() === null` fallbacks).

findings.issue: Sprite URLs are reconstructed from a hardcoded pattern while the artwork path uses the API-provided URL (api.ts:191) — two sources of truth for media; if the API's sprite layout moves, cards break independently.
findings.suggestion: Derive from sprites.front_default when a pokemon record is already fetched, and keep the pattern only as a documented fallback for the species list.

findings.issue: The nested Show/fallback (`Show when={data()} fallback={<Show when={data() === null}>…}`) encodes loading vs. not-found implicitly and is copy-pasted across four routes.
findings.suggestion: Extract one `<RouteData data={…}>{(d) => …}</RouteData>` wrapper that renders NotFound on null and Suspense otherwise.

findings.issue: `padding-right: var(--space-3) !important` is used to out-specify the app's own `.stats-table td` rule.
findings.suggestion: Use a `.stats-table td.stat-value` selector instead of !important.

findings.issue: `typeof process !== "undefined"` guard in a module that is explicitly server-only ("use server" queries); it is dead noise and slightly obscures the intent.
findings.suggestion: Read process.env.API_BASE_URL directly and keep the module out of client code via the "use server" boundary.

findings.issue: Every move record for every version group of a Pokémon is fetched and serialized to the client even though only one game is shown at a time; the shared cache makes it cheap on the server but the payload grows with move count.
findings.suggestion: Consider passing the selected game into the query so only that game's rows are serialized; the version-group list itself stays small.

summary: A cleanly modern SolidStart v2 app: vite.config-based setup, query/"use server"/createAsync/preload data loading, router 1.x and vite 8 — all verified against the current v2 docs and npm, with a minimal six-dependency set that is exactly what the framework requires. The debt is all in rigor rather than currency: an untyped any-everywhere data layer with no typecheck tooling means the strict tsconfig never runs. Fixing the types boundary and adding a 404 status would make this a codebase you'd point others to.
